properties.title: Special Marine Warning issued November 20 at 1:34PM EST until November 20 at 2:30PM EST by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
SMWJAX

The National Weather Service in Jacksonville has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Waters from Fernandina Beach to St. Augustine FL from 20 to 60
NM...
Waters from St. Augustine to Flagler Beach FL from 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 230 PM EST.

* At 134 PM EST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 38 nm east of Daytona Beach Shores, or 39
nm east of South Daytona, moving north at 20 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts to 45 knots.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* The severe thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued November 20 at 9:20AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor is forecast to continue to rise through
Moderate Flood Stage, reaching Major Flood Stage early next week due
to heavy rainfall working its way through the basin in combination
with strong north-northeast flow.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering
many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration
flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return
below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road
becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous
homes on Wildhog, Possum, and Bonnet roads. Roads along Blue Creek
are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter, Branch and
Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EST Friday the stage was 3.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EST Friday was 3.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 3.8 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EST.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Extreme rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River has
caused the river near Cocoa to rise through Major Flood Stage, well
above its previous record flood stage. The river level will continue
a slow rise through tonight and is expected to become steady this
weekend into early next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w, Above Lake Harney,
Sanford, Deland, Astor...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park

impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass

Fish Camp.

- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending

- Forecast...The river is forecast to slowly rise to 18.8 feet on
Saturday and remain steady near that level into early next week.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
